summary: One member’s change of caucus puts the other party in charge of the chamber.
realLife: Tom Daschle regained the US Senate majority leadership in 2001 when Vermont’s Jim Jeffords left the Republican caucus.
inGame: needs: a caucus change linked to the chamber's organizing vote.

turns.what: The member leaves the party but still votes with the old caucus to organize.
turns.pulledBy: An existing leadership agreement covers committee assignments.
turns.writesBack: The party roster changes and the same leader keeps the floor.

turns.what: The new caucus takes control at the next organizing session.
turns.pulledBy: The chamber is in recess when the member switches.
turns.writesBack: The leadership change takes effect when members return.
